problem: The Hogan annotations state that the figure of about fifty bodies in the village came from the Irgun officer's account in the memorandum (with about 20 in no-man's land and about 150 in a pit he could not verify), though de Reynier later reported having seen fifty. fix.digest: Two days after Irgun and Lehi forces took the village of Deir Yassin, de Reynier went there with a man who said he was an Irgun officer, two ambulances, two doctors and five or six Magen David Adom nurses. The commander told him there were about 200 dead and no wounded, and that about 150 women and children had surrendered. The memorandum gives the officer's account of about fifty bodies in the village, about twenty in no-man's land and about 150 in a pit, which de Reynier could not verify; he later reported having seen about fifty himself. He found a girl of about ten alive but comatose and had her taken away by ambulance, and he gave instructions for burial with lists of names.
fix.source_note: De Reynier's memorandum to the ICRC, Geneva, dated 13 April 1948, in Matthew Hogan's annotated English translation (1999). Death tolls are contested: the figure the Irgun gave him (about 200) was widely repeated in 1948; the translator's annotations, and later Israeli and Palestinian researchers, give about 100–110 for the whole village.

fix.digest: Consul General Macdonald relayed to Washington Ralph Bunche's message that Bernadotte had been assassinated in the Katamon quarter while driving in a three-car convoy from Government House to the YMCA. Men in Jewish Army uniforms got out of an Israeli Army type jeep at a road block and fired at point-blank range; the French observer Colonel André Sérot was killed and Bernadotte died soon after reaching hospital. Israeli military and civilian leaders expressed regret and promised to hunt the gunmen. The next day the consulate reported that the Stern group was generally assumed responsible.

fix.digest: Ralph Bunche, now acting Mediator, reported that the convoy flew UN and white flags and had no armed protection, that a jeep similar in colour to those of the Israeli army blocked the road, and that one man fired several bursts into the Mediator's car while two others fired to cover the assault. He relayed the Israeli Foreign Minister's statement that a group calling itself Hazit Hamoledet, an arm of the Stern group (Lehi), had claimed the killing, and held the Provisional Government of Israel responsible for what he called a breach of the truce of the utmost gravity.
